newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sets up border task-force against diseases.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sets up border task-force against diseases.

text.p: Algeria is to deploy border task forces to protect its people from rampant diseases in African countries to the south.

Health Minister Yahia Guidoum announced on Monday that a National Committee of Medical Control at Borders had been set up and would oversee setting up control services at borders to guard against diseases such as AIDS and meningitis.
The committee comprises representatives from the trade and transport ministries, police and customs, said the official Algerian news agency APS, reporting the minister's decision.

"The decision is motivated by the rampant epidemiological situation in some neighbouring countries to southern Algeria and which caused transmission of serious diseases, mostly AIDS, paludism and meningitis," said Guidoum quoted by APS.
The committee must also draw a programme to combat diseases at borders and oversee the setting up of an information network to keep watch on diseases in southern countries neighbouring Algeria.
"The lack of a health control system and a sanitary police at borders has brought the reappearance of serious diseases such as malaria and meningitis," said Guidoum.
Tens of thousands of refugees settled in southern Algeria in 1980s and 1990s fleeing droughts and violence in neighbouring Mali and Niger.
Niger is one of the countries to have reported serious outbreaks of meningitis this year.
